value.rationale: A natural question in numerically approximated invariant-measure calibration is whether independent stationary samples at one or two simulator resolutions identify the underlying dissipative linear diffusion parameters. The full inverse-fiber geometry shows exponential or continuous ambiguity even with noise strength known; a second resolution resolves unknown drift and noise exactly, while the exact OU stationary law and nonsymmetric Euler variants retain genuine nonidentifiability. The result supplies an exact two-resolution experimental-design and feasibility certificate with a sharp noise-amplification denominator. This is a structural characterization motivated by inverse numerical statistics, not an arbitrary isolated numerical example or a claim that the elementary scalar AR(1) formula is novel.
